evidence: M-O s.v. pollution, citing Egger: inquinātiōne āëris
terms.comment: Lewis & Short has the noun only in the Vulgate (Sap. 14.26), of the defiling of souls; the modern sense rests on the classical verb.

evidence: Ov. M. 14.56: venēnīs, of poisoning a pool (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The classical way to say it: āēr inquinātus, aqua inquināta. Also figurative, to stain a reputation (Cic.).
Late Latin, and in Christian authors of moral or ritual defilement; use inquinātiō.

phrases.latin: oleam quam prīmum ex terrā tollitō. sī inquināta erit, lavātō ā foliīs et stercore pūrgātō
phrases.english: pick the olives up off the ground at once; if they are dirty, wash them and clean off the leaves and muck

sources: Lewis & Short: inquinatio · Lewis & Short: inquino · Lewis & Short: pollutio
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. pollution.
